translations.title: Why does copying only DeepMimic's imitation reward often fail on long, dynamic skills?
translations.answer: DeepMimic becomes learnable through the combination of phase-conditioned imitation, reference-state initialization (RSI), and early termination (ET); task reward then drives outcomes such as throwing or obstacle crossing. Reproductions must report tracking and task success separately, and simulated-character evidence cannot be promoted directly to humanoid hardware capability.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Reference motions are retargeted and physically meaningful for the simulated character.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Phase synchronization is valid or explicitly monitored.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Simulated dynamic motion imitation and task-augmented skills
translations.applicability.robots.0: Simulated characters in the paper; robot hardware requires a separate feasibility and sim-to-real layer
translations.applicability.simulators.0: Bullet/DeepMimic and equivalent physics simulators with matched state, PD, and contacts
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper's method, RSI/ET ablations, and task-versus-imitation table directly support the claim, and pinned official code exposes phase, reward, termination, and PD interfaces. Confidence is capped because all principal evidence is simulated-character rather than robot hardware evidence.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines phase-conditioned imitation, RSI, ET, and separate imitation/task outcomes with controlled ablations.
